description: SPI idle-state pulls at the module
notes: SIX, not three - BOTH SIDES of the 74AHCT125. Cable side: CS pulled UP, SCLK and MOSI to ground, so the buffer's inputs do not float and crowbar when the instrument is absent. DAC side: same, because with OE disabled the buffer outputs are Hi-Z and it is then the DAC's SCLK/DIN/SYNC that float - which is the state these were bought for and the three cable-side pulls do not reach. Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault; a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC. CABLE-SIDE CS PULLS TO 3V3: pulled to 5V it drives 430uA continuously through the unpowered ESP32's input clamp in the design's NORMAL resting state, and the node sits at ~0.7V so 'CS idle high' is not even achieved. DAC-SIDE CS PULLS TO AVDD (the LM317's 5.21V), not bus +5V - a pull-up belongs on its consumer's rail, and on the bus rail a reversed ribbon reaches the DAC's SYNC pin and turns a $0.30 buffer failure into a DAC failure *** ONE OF THE SIX IS NOT PLACEABLE YET: 3V3 EXISTS ONLY AT THE INSTRUMENT END. *** The module makes +/-12V, bus +5V and DAC AVDD, and the umbilical carries no 3V3, so the cable-side CS pull is either an instrument-end part or it needs a rail this board does not have. Lay out the other five; hold that one until digital-and-supervision.md's Still open settles which end it sits at

description: Series termination on SCLK, MOSI and CS at the driving end
notes: THREE. 100R, not 220R. *** 2m OF CAT5 IS A 100-OHM TRANSMISSION LINE (20ns round trip against 2-5ns edges), NOT AN RC CORNER *** - three reviewers agreed independently that the old RC derivation was simply the wrong model, so do not re-derive this one from a corner frequency. At 220R the far end's first step is 1.83-1.86V against the 74AHCT125's 2.0V VIH, dwelling ~20ns per edge in the forbidden band on a part with no hysteresis. 100R gives a clean 2.75V single step and 33mA of fault current; 68R is electrically ideal but draws 48mA against a 40mA pad spec

description: ESD protection on the umbilical's SPI lines
notes: SCLK, MOSI, CS (+ one spare channel) to PWR_GND. ORDER CODE IS SP0504BAHTG AND IT IS SOT-23-5, NOT SOT-23-6 [SP0504BAHT.pdf p.1 ordering table, package outlines pp.6-7]; SP0505BAHTG is the SOT-23-6 part and brings a fifth channel if one is wanted. *** THE PART HAS NO PULSE RATING AT ALL. *** Eight pages carry no I_PP, no 8/20us or 10/1000us waveform, no surge curve and no theta-JA: it is ESD-rated only (IEC 61000-4-2, 20kV contact / 30kV air). What it does specify is a steady-state ceiling - package dissipation 0.225 W [Abs Max p.2, corroborated 'PD@70degC .225W' p.7]. SO A SUSTAINED FAULT IS NOT SURVIVED BY A BIGGER ARRAY; the fix is a series resistor or a resettable element. ALL FOUR CHANNELS SHARE ONE COMMON PIN (pin 2), to PWR_GND at J-UMB. U-TVS-CHAIN is a second package because it clamps at the J-CHAIN, elsewhere on the main board. THE ARRAY IS EFFECTIVELY UNI-DIRECTIONAL: the -0.8V negative clamp is a forward diode drop, not an avalanche knee. Fine for 0-3.3V SPI; MUST NOT be reused on a bipolar CV node. 30 pF per channel is high for a modern array - against 2 m of Cat5 and R-SPI-SER that is ~29 ns of edge on a 250 ns half-period at 2 MHz, acceptable, and it is the only TVS term in the umbilical edge budget. DO NOT RE-PROPOSE onsemi ESD7104: it is a clean 4-channel 5V array on paper and ships only in UDFN10 and WDFNW10, leadless fine pitch, banned by the ADR 0013 package policy - as was SP3012-06UTG before it. Two parts have now been rejected for that one reason

description: Joins the umbilical adapter (PCB-UMB-ADAPTER) to the main board's tongue: soldered into both, no mated contacts
notes: PINOUT IS umbilical-pinmap, PIN N = etherCON PIN N: the adapter runs each of J-UMBILICAL-INST's pins straight to the same-numbered pin here, so 'J-UMB pin N' on any page is the same conductor as J-UMBILICAL pin N. FITTED: the short legs through the adapter from its rear face, the long legs down through the main board's tongue; solder both, then trim the legs that stand in front of the adapter. The row meets the adapter between the etherCON's G tab and its peg line - mechanical/drc.echo 'J-UMB's row lands on the adapter clear of the etherCON's footprint'. RATING: one pin carries +12V (umbilical-current) and one PWR_GND; rate them above the module's current-limit trip (R-ILIM, hardware/module/umbilical-load-switch/), not the typical draw - the worst case is an overload just under the trip, carried indefinitely. A 2.54mm header pin is ~3A [from memory], above the etherCON's own 1.5A per contact [ds], which is the limit here. D-REVSHUNT and U-TVS-SPI sit at it. PIN 8 (DIG_GND) TIES TO THE MAIN BOARD'S GROUND (PWR_GND) AT THIS HEADER (ADR 0018): a short, wide connection at the pin. Route SCLK, MOSI and CS_MOD from the MCU side of J-MCU to here over unbroken ground, and keep AGND_SENSE (pin 2) off this return. The module end is dig-gnd-topology, still disputed. PART NUMBER OPEN: any 1 x 8 2.54mm right-angle header; its insulator and row height are config/body.yaml boards.umb_joint_*, from memory until M4
